newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Sit cross-legged and bounce, EU leaders told.
newsitem.headline: Sit cross-legged and bounce, EU leaders told.

text.p: As European leaders struggled to reach agreement on EMU and find solutions to the problems of crime, unemployment and ethnic conflict, another Dublin summit told them it had the answer -- sit cross-legged and bounce.

Leaders of Europe's Natural Law parties, meeting in Dublin on Friday, said all the problems facing the European Union could be solved through meditation and "yogic flying", which involves springing around while sitting with legs crossed.

Crime and unemployment could be eliminated, conflicts in regions like Northern Ireland solved and Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) painlessly achieved, they said, if a crack EU team of 7,000 yogic fliers was created to generate harmony and raise the Union's collective consciousness.

"They would neutralise the stress, negativity, and frustration that has been collected in the consciousness of the whole of Europe," said Reinhard Borowitz, Secretary General of the Maharishi European Council of Natural Law Parties.
"They will be like a task force to clean up the mental pollution that 465 million EU citizens produce every day," he told a news conference.
Borowitz said the summit of EU leaders taking place just one km away in Dublin Castle would find no answers to the challenges facing Europe.

"We are meeting for our summit here because we believe it is extremely important that solutions are offered to the urgent problems that exist in the EU," he said. "The solutions tried or offered at the EU Council are simply not good enough."

Geoffrey Clements, leader of Britain's Natural Law Party, said EU leaders were doomed in their attempts to create a single currency because they failed to understand the principles of currency markets and were adopting the wrong approach.

Rather than trying to manipulate currencies, the EU should aim to achieve harmony at the level of individuals, businesses and countries. This would create harmony in currency markets and allow a single European currency to be established, he said.

The Natural Law Party was founded in 1992 in Britain and says it is now established in 44 countries and active in a further eight. It has taken part in elections in several countries, with "varying results" according to Borowitz.
